summary: Short-lived tenant hogging triggers autoscaler miss and batched-job saturation
description:
Issue summary: Customer TextFlow.ai observed sudden P50->P99 latency degradation and diminished sustained throughput in their dedicated capacity pool. Impact: production traffic experienced 20-40% throughput collapse for 6 minute windows and multiple 5xxs during burst windows. The pattern repeats during short-lived spikey workloads from other tenants. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west-2, mixed GPU types, tenant pinned to reserved pool with burst permissions.

Observed behavior: During short bursts from several tenants doing many small streaming requests ( < 300 tokens ), autoscaler did not provision new GPU slots fast enough and the serving-runtime showed NVLink and kernel-queue saturation. Symptoms resemble noisy-neighbor GPU hogging combined with slot fragmentation and autoscaler scale-up lag.

Customer reported at 2026-03-10 14:02 PDT; support ticket opened 2026-03-10 14:12.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated pool with mixed A40 and A100 instances and allow burst reservations.
2) Have several tenants (simulated) send high-rate short streaming requests (50-300 tokens) for 3-6 minutes in overlapping windows.
3) Observe autoscaler behaviour when queue length grows and GPU slot allocation latency (metrics: autoscaler.scale_up_latency).
4) Monitor serving-runtime logs for kernel queue depth, nvlink utilization, and batcher slot fragmentation.
5) Observe client-facing throughput and 5xx counts under load (token throughput per GPU drops and p99 latency spikes).
logs_and_metrics: Attached: partial grafana snapshots (panel ids: dedicated_pool_uswest_23, autoscaler_lag_7), serving-runtime traces, and tail of worker logs. Key metrics: p99 latency rose from 140ms -> 1.2s, avg token/s per GPU dropped 35%, kernel-queue length spiked 6x, NVLink utilization peaked, GPU allocation wait time increased from 200ms to 1.8s. Error patterns: increased "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" and "INTERNAL_KERNEL_FAILURE" in logs during high fanout. Linked grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pool/dedicated-uswest?view=spike
timeline: 2026-03-10 14:02 PDT - Customer reports intermittent 5xx and large p99 spikes during morning traffic window.
2026-03-10 14:12 PDT - Support ticket created (SUP-823999) by Maya; initial triage notes added.
2026-03-10 14:25 PDT - SRE notified; began live telemetry collection and enabled verbose batcher logging.
2026-03-10 15:05 PDT - Temporary workaround applied: limit tenant burst concurrency to 8 streams and enable strict slot preemption for bursts.
2026-03-10 16:30 PDT - Observed partial recovery after workaround; throughput restored to ~85% of baseline but p99 still elevated during microbursts.
2026-03-11 09:00 PDT - Engineering confirmed autoscaler slow-path underestimates short-lived slot demand (investigation opened).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler decision loop uses moving-window metrics that smooth short spikes, causing underprovisioning for brief high-fanout events.
Hypothesis 2: Mixed GPU heterogeneity caused slot fragmentation; short streams created many small batches that failed to amortize kernel startup costs.
Data: Correlation between tenant burst origin IP ranges and kernel-queue spikes from 14:01-14:07; NVLink logs show high intra-node transfer during these windows.
SRE actions: captured heap snapshots from batcher, enabled per-tenant counters, and reproduced locally with a replay harness (see PR linked).
Preliminary: Autoscaler scale_up_latency is higher when scale decisions coincide with many small in-flight streams; scale decisions are delayed by average_window=120s config.
Related: Similar mechanism referenced in SUP-417325 but root cause there was different (background checkpoint writer).
comments: Maya Thompson (Support) 2026-03-10 14:15: Thanks for the report. I've requested live graphs and asked for customer traffic samples. Noted customer is on dedicated plan with burst permissions.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10 14:30: Investigating; enabling verbose batcher and autoscaler debug. Early look: kernel queue and NVLink show spikes concurrent with reported windows.

Customer (TextFlow.ai - Leah Park) 2026-03-10 14:37: We observed these drops only during other tenants' short bursts; our workload is steady. Appreciate action — this is impacting production conversions.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10 15:10: Applied emergency mitigation: per-tenant burst concurrency cap and aggressive preemption for short streams. Asking engineering to evaluate autoscaler smoothing window reduction.

Alex Chen (Infra Eng) 2026-03-11 09:12: Reproduced locally with harness -> autoscaler averaging window 120s causes delayed scale decisions for bursts < 60s. Draft PR to introduce short-burst fast-path in autoscaler linked.
Support (Maya) 2026-03-11 10:05: Customer confirmed partial improvement after mitigation but reports intermittent p99 during high fanout. Keeping ticket open until rollout to prod confirmed.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-10 15:05): per-tenant burst concurrency limit = 8, enable aggressive slot preemption for streams < 400 tokens. Customer throughput recovered to ~85% baseline and 5xxs dropped.
Medium-term engineering fix: autoscaler fast-path PR implemented to detect short-lived high-fanout events and apply expedited scale decisions (PR #219).

Code changes: autoscaler change reduces smoothing window for short-burst detection and introduces transient_slot_reservation to reduce allocation latency (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/219).
Additional mitigation: scheduler to prefer homogeneous GPU packing for burst reservations to avoid NVLink contention; follow-up task created in INT-3301.

Postmortem: Boarded for 2026-03-17 retrospective; action items include improved per-tenant burst governance, autoscaler unit tests for microburst scenarios, and metrics dashboard for short-burst signals.
Status: fix merged to canary 2026-03-12, scheduled for full prod rollout 2026-03-15 pending observability checks. Customer notified and will be updated when prod rollout completes.
